> 外物不可必，故龍逢誅，比干戮，箕子狂，惡來死，桀紂亡。

External things cannot be made certain. Therefore: 關龍逢 executed, 比干 cut open, 箕子 driven to feign madness, 惡來 killed, 桀 and 紂 destroyed.

Five names in one line, and the list is the argument: three loyal, two vicious, all the same outcome.

## 必 is the only thing on trial

必: certain, necessary, guaranteed.

The chapter does not argue that the world is unfair. It argues that the word 必 does not apply — and then spends its length showing what happens to people who build on it.

## 忠未必信, 孝未必愛

Loyalty does not guarantee trust: 伍員 floated down the river, 萇弘 died in Shu.

Filial piety does not guarantee love: 孝己 worried himself to death, 曾參 grieved.

Note the structure. Both sentences grant the virtue and deny the return. The virtue is real; the guarantee is not.

## 藏其血三年而化為碧

His blood was kept three years and turned to jade.

This is the most extravagant image in the book, and it is not decoration: loyalty at its extreme will not even let its blood decay. Read literally it is impossible; read as a claim about people it is exact — some commitments do not dissolve on schedule.

## 木與木相摩而然，金與火相守則流

Two pieces of wood rubbed together catch fire; metal and fire kept together melt.

Structural, not moral. These sentences say: some outcomes follow from what the two things are, and have nothing to do with who you are. The chapter's comfort is thin and honest — most of what happened to you was never about you.

## 水中有火，乃焚大槐

Fire inside water burns the great locust tree. The image for the anomalous, kept without explanation.

## 焚和: two characters, the heaviest in the chapter

焚: to burn. 和: the condition in which things hold without harming each other.

To burn 和 is the chapter's final charge — worse than any single failure, because it destroys the medium in which anything can be held.

## 月固不勝火

Moonlight was never a match for fire.

No consolation offered, and that is the point: clarity and gentleness do not defeat force. This is one of the few sentences in the book that refuses to be comforting.

## 涸轍之鮒: the fish in the dried rut

A fish asks for water; the answer is that the speaker will go and divert a river for it. The reply: 吾失我常與，我無所處 — I have lost what I was ordinarily with, and have nowhere to be.

常與: the thing one is always with. The fish is not asking for a river. It is asking for its ordinary condition, and the offer of a future grand solution is a refusal.

枯魚之肆: the dried-fish market. That is where the delay ends.

## The test

Name one thing you are counting on as certain — a return, a recognition, a fairness. Then apply 必: on what basis is it guaranteed? If the honest answer is "because I did the right thing," the chapter has five names and a fish for you.
